visual_text: Six months after a booklet on tablet risks
People aged 65 to 95 who had taken benzodiazepines for a long time. Stopped means no more pharmacy refills.
Booklet and a plan for cutting down: about 27 in 100 had stopped
Usual care: about 5 in 100 had stopped
Tannenbaum et al., JAMA Intern Med 2014: 303 people, Quebec community pharmacies
Ask your pharmacist for written information on the risks and a slow, agreed plan for cutting down.
29 of 77 people who tried to taper in a second Quebec trial reported withdrawal symptoms; none needed hospital care
Both trials ran through community pharmacies in Quebec
Mailing information did not reduce use of high-risk medicines (including sedatives) in a large US trial in people with dementia
Martin et al., JAMA 2018; Singh et al., JAMA Intern Med 2024
alt_text: Two grids of 100 person icons. After a booklet on tablet risks and a plan for cutting down, about 27 in 100 older long-term benzodiazepine users had stopped at 6 months, against about 5 in 100 with usual care. 303 people aged 65 to 95, Quebec pharmacies.

Read it with care. 29 of 77 people who tried to taper in a second Quebec trial reported withdrawal symptoms; none needed hospital care. Both trials were in Quebec pharmacies. Mailing information did not reduce high-risk medicine use in a US trial in dementia. Ask your pharmacist for written information and a slow plan.
